Higher caution advised day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Sussex Police recorded 1,686 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 31.8 per 1,000 residents, the 2nd highest rate of Brighton and Hove's 21 wards. The daytime score here is driven by shoplifting (130), drugs (18), vehicle crime (11); the evening/night score by anti social behaviour (137), violent crime (122), public order (44). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is St. Peter's and North Laine safe?

Wandroz currently rates St. Peter's and North Laine in Brighton and Hove as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Brighton and Hove during the day and an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Brighton and Hove at night. This rating is derived from Sussex Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is St. Peter's and North Laine safe at night?

At night, St. Peter's and North Laine is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Brighton and Hove. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is St. Peter's and North Laine a good area to stay in as a tourist?

St. Peter's and North Laine's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Brighton and Hove) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
